---
title: "Recall"
description: "The fraction of actual positive cases that a classifier correctly identifies."
term: "Recall"
letter: "R"
category: "Model Evaluation"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

Recall answers: “Of all the cases that really were positive, how many did
the model find?” High recall is important when missing a positive case is
costly.

## Technical explanation

For binary classification, recall (also called sensitivity or true-positive
rate) is $\mathrm{TP}/(\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN})$, where TP is true positives
and FN is false negatives. The metric depends on the classification
threshold and the definition of the positive class.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

In screening, safety alerts, or defect detection, false negatives may carry
high costs. Recall should be considered alongside precision, error costs,
and the workload caused by false positives.

## How it works

Choose a threshold, compare predictions with labeled outcomes, and divide
correctly detected positives by all actual positives. Lowering a threshold
often increases recall while also increasing false positives; select an
operating point using validation data and domain constraints.

## Practical example

If 90 of 100 actual defective items are flagged, recall is $90/100=0.9$,
or 90%. This says nothing by itself about how many flagged items were
actually defective; precision measures that.

## Common misconceptions

- Recall is not the fraction of model predictions that are correct; that
  relates to precision.
- A recall of 100% can be achieved by flagging every case, which may be
  operationally useless.
